Section: section_1 — The Leap from Concrete to Abstract

Lecture lines:
Vectors are arrows in 2D space. [Asset: arrow]
Space acts like a system of rules. [Asset: rules]
Abstract objects follow these exact rules. [Asset: objects]
We generalize beyond 2D coordinate grids. [Asset: grid]
Vector spaces define this unified structure. [Asset: structure]

Planned animations:
Display a single point (Dot) at center (#FF5733) labeled 'Object'.
Fade in a set of arrows pointing to the point, labeled 'Relationships' (#33FF57).
Transform the collection of arrows into a abstract vector space symbol (#3357FF).
Flash the symbol to emphasize its abstract nature (#FFFFFF).
Fade out, leaving only the symbol (#3357FF).

Section: section_2 — The Rules of the Game: Defining Vector Spaces

Lecture lines:
Vector addition combines two ingredients. [Asset: add]
Scalar multiplication scales our ingredients. [Asset: scale]
Closure means the result stays valid. [Asset: closure]
We check eight required axioms. [Asset: axioms]
The system is a vector space. [Asset: space]

Planned animations:
Draw a set of objects on screen labeled 'Elements' (#FFFF00).
Show a rule connecting two elements labeled 'Addition' (#FF00FF).
Show a rule multiplying an element by a scalar labeled 'Scaling' (#00FFFF).

Section: section_3 — Case Study: Beyond Geometric Arrows

Lecture lines:
Polynomials behave just like geometric vectors. [Asset: poly]
Functions also follow vector space rules. [Asset: func]
Zero polynomial acts as our zero. [Asset: zero]
Algebraic structure defines both categories. [Asset: structure]
Abstraction links disparate mathematical objects. [Asset: link]

Planned animations:
Draw a polynomial function graph labeled 'P(x)' (#FF9900).
Display the coefficients as a vector [a, b, c] (#99FF00).
Animate the vector components morphing into the function's graph (#FF9900).

Section: section_4 — Visualizing Abstract Dimensions

Lecture lines:
Dimension counts our necessary basis elements. [Asset: basis]
Pixels build a full image character. [Asset: image]
Linear combinations create the final object. [Asset: linear]
Changing coefficients shifts the result. [Asset: shift]
Basis defines the space's internal dimensionality. [Asset: dim]

Planned animations:
Draw a grid representing 2D space (#AAAAAA).
Transform the grid into a 3D perspective to hint at dimension (#FFFFFF).
Represent the abstract vector as a glowing dot in the 3D space (#FF00FF).

Section: section_5 — Summary and Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
Abstract spaces unify diverse data types. [Asset: unify]
Geometry applies to signals and weights. [Asset: app]
Mathematical toolboxes solve complex problems. [Asset: tools]

Planned animations:
Show a real-world system (e.g., a data network) (#00FF00).
Overlay the vector space model onto the network elements (#FFFFFF).
Pulse the network nodes to show how the model predicts behavior (#FF0000).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        )
        self.wait(2)
